title: Message-format and datalink translation gateway (commercial mesh/TAK to Link 16/VMF for small units and drones; LLM/ontology translation between USMTF, ADatP-3, MIP, VMF, NVG and CoT)
problem: Small units and Replicator-class drones on commercial MANET/TAK cannot push tracks and targets into Link 16/VMF-based fires and air C2 without a hardware gateway, a handheld Link 16 radio or voice relay, and coalition systems speaking USMTF/ADatP-3/MIP/VMF/NVG/CoT are re-bridged with one-off translators at every exercise.

user.exact_role: Fires cell NCO / fire support officer, JTAC, small-UAS operator and air battle manager who must move a track from a TAK/mesh screen into AFATDS, a VMF-capable terminal or the Link 16 picture; and the C2 integration engineer at Bold Quest/CWIX/Project Convergence who stands up the bridge
user.echelon: Company to brigade fires; air component battle management; coalition exercise integration
organization_examples: Army BCT fires cells and TiC brigades (4th ID, 25th ID NGC2 units)
USAF/USMC JTACs using ATAK as a DACAS toolkit
CENTCOM Task Forces 59/99/179 (low-cost UAS, target information sharing)
Joint Staff J6/JDAT Bold Quest, NATO CWIX integration cells
Replicator ADA2 system integrators under DIU ORIENT

current_workflow: 1. Drone or dismount track appears as a CoT event in ATAK/TAK Server over commercial MANET (Persistent, Silvus, Doodle).
2. Operator reads grid/track and passes it by voice or chat to the fires cell or air battle manager.
3. Fires cell re-enters the target in AFATDS or composes a VMF nine-line on a VMF-capable terminal; air C2 re-enters it into the Link 16 picture via a terminal or ADSI-class gateway.
4. Where a hardware bridge exists (BACN aircraft, BATS-D handheld, ADSI/JRE gateway, V2X Gateway Mission Router) the translation is done by that box, which is scarce, program-owned and crypto-keyed.
5. At coalition events an integration cell configures point-to-point translators (ASCA, CoT gateway for SitaWare, MIP/NVG/ADatP-3 adapters) per exercise; results are not retained as a product.
current_solution: Government-owned and commercial gateways already exist at every layer: Ultra I&C ADSI (CoT-to-JREAP-C translation, 21 legacy instances unified into one baseline - company claim), L3Harris BATS-D handheld Link 16 radio with ATAK/ADSI/CoT support, Curtiss-Wright TDL translation gateway, V2X Gateway Mission Router (Army, $48.5M award 2024, company PR), BSI VMF Gateway plugin for MACE, Northrop BACN aircraft, Fuse Integration ABMS networking pods, ATAK-MIL radio drivers for Link 16 gateways, Systematic SitaWare with built-in USMTF/ADatP-3/MIP/NVG/ASCA support and a CoT gateway, and Raft Data Platform transformation/federation inside the NGC2 common data layer baseline (June 2026).
failure: It fails at the seam, not in translation logic: (a) the translator must sit behind a certified Link 16/MIDS terminal with crypto, and the terminal owner (prime/program office) controls that interface; (b) MIL-STD-6016 is Distribution C and AECA/ITAR-restricted, so a non-cleared, partly non-U.S.-person team cannot legally obtain the message standard; (c) at coalition level the bottleneck is releasability, accreditation and interface access, so translators demonstrated at CWIX/Bold Quest do not transition; (d) no program office buys 'a translator' - it is bought as a feature of a terminal, a gateway box, a C2 suite or the NGC2 data layer.

evidence.claim: MIL-STD-6016 (Link 16 message standard) contains technical data whose export is restricted under the Arms Export Control Act; distribution is C (federal government and contractors only); allied release requires foreign disclosure authorization; contractors obtain it through a government POC via ASSIST.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: L3Harris BATS-D is a handheld Link 16 radio marketed with ATAK/TAK support, ADSI integration, Link 16 CMI compliance and Cursor on Target capability - i.e., the dismount-to-Link 16 bridge already exists as certified hardware.
evidence.source_title: Battlefield Awareness and Targeting System - Dismounted (BATS-D) brochure
evidence.label: FACT (company brochure; performance not independently verified)

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: They have, repeatedly, at the prototype level, and the market absorbed the capability into terminals (BATS-D), gateway boxes (ADSI, GMR, Curtiss-Wright), C2 suites (SitaWare) and the NGC2 data layer (Raft). A standalone translator has no requirement owner: the Link 16 side needs a certified terminal, crypto and JITC MIL-STD-6016 conformance testing that only the terminal/gateway program can sponsor; the coalition side stalls on releasability, accreditation and interface access rather than schema mapping. LLM/ontology mapping lowers a cost that was never the constraint, and introduces non-determinism into safety-critical fires messages that JITC conformance testing would reject.
technical_wedge: Honest answer: none as a standalone product. The only sliver a two-founder team could build is the unclassified half - a CoT/TAK-side adapter and conformance-test kit (CoT <-> MIP/JC3IEDM, NVG, ADatP-3/USMTF, ASCA, STANAG 4586 for drone OEMs) with deterministic, schema-verified mapping and an LLM used only to draft mappings for human review - and that sliver belongs inside another gap's edge-bridge product (S08-G2) or inside NATO INSPECT-style continuous conformance tooling, not as a gateway business.

mvp.what: Open-standards adapter service: ATAK-CIV plugin + TAK Server bridge that converts CoT events to/from public coalition formats (USMTF/MIL-STD-6040, MIP/JC3IEDM, NVG, ADatP-3 subset) with schema-validated deterministic transforms and an offline LLM-assisted mapping editor; Link 16 represented only by a synthetic, non-controlled J-series-like schema (no MIL-STD-6016 content).
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the unclassified half: live TAK clients on a commercial mesh exchanging tracks with an open MIP/NVG consumer (e.g., an FMN-style test harness) with round-trip fidelity metrics. No for the Link 16/VMF half, which cannot be demonstrated credibly without a certified terminal and controlled specs.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That a deterministic adapter reaches conformance-grade fidelity (zero silent field loss, correct classification/releasability markings carried) and that any program office or allied OEM would pay for it separately from SitaWare/Raft/ADSI - the second proof is the one that has historically failed.

data_requirement.what: Message standards (MIL-STD-6016 Link 16 - Distribution C/ITAR; MIL-STD-6017 VMF - distribution-controlled; MIL-STD-6040 USMTF - public; ADatP-3 - NATO controlled; MIP/JC3IEDM, NVG, CoT - public), Link 16 network design and crypto interfaces, and representative message traffic for testing.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Public formats (CoT, USMTF, MIP, NVG) yes. MIL-STD-6016/6017 only via a government POC for a U.S. contractor on a sponsored effort; allied release requires foreign disclosure authorization. A non-U.S.-person co-founder would likely need to be walled off from 6016 technical data (export-control counsel required). Live Link 16 traffic: not obtainable without a program sponsor.
sources: MIP/JC3IEDM and NVG public specifications (NATO/MIP community)

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: They already have it: L3Harris owns the certified handheld terminal; Anduril/Raft own the NGC2 transformation baseline and Lattice Mesh; Systematic ships multi-standard gateways; ADSI is the joint standard gateway. Adding an LLM-assisted mapping editor to any of these is a quarter's work for an incumbent team with spec access.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: REJECT. There is no interface a startup controls, no data it uniquely holds, and the safety-critical nature of fires messages favors deterministic, certified incumbents over an LLM-based newcomer.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Link 16 message standards and network designs are AECA/ITAR-controlled technical data with Distribution C; gateways require JITC MIL-STD-6016 conformance testing, crypto handling and an ATO under a program of record; VMF is distribution-controlled; coalition releases require foreign disclosure authorization.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian co-founder who is not a U.S. person would very likely need to be excluded from all Link 16/VMF technical data (deemed-export), which removes the business/product founder from the core product; SBIR ownership tests and any future FOCI mitigation add further constraints. Requires export-control and immigration counsel; no legal determination made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Link 16, VMF, USMTF and ADatP-3 have no civilian users; the generic schema-translation engine competes with mature commercial iPaaS/ETL tools where an LLM mapping assistant is a feature, not a company. Only the CoT/TAK side (public safety, SAR, wildfire) has a thin civilian analogue.

defensibility.explanation: The only durable assets in this category are conformance certifications and program-of-record positions, both of which accrue to the terminal/gateway owner and the data-layer prime rather than to a translation-software vendor; mappings themselves are commodity.

why_now: Replicator/NGC2 multiply non-Link 16 endpoints (commercial MANET drones and TAK clients) and NGC2 moved to a common data layer in June 2026, so there is more traffic to bridge; LLMs make schema-mapping drafts cheap. But the constraint moved with it: the Army assigned transformation to Raft/Anduril, DIU is buying network topology (ORIENT), and the Link 16 side remains hardware-and-certification bound - so 'why now' is stronger for the incumbents than for a new entrant.
killer_risk: No PROBLEM->USER->REQUIREMENT OWNER->PROGRAM OFFICE->CONTRACTING OFFICE->BUDGET->VEHICLE path exists for a standalone translator; the Link 16 half is legally closed to this team (ITAR/Distribution C plus a non-U.S.-person founder) and the unclassified half is already covered by government-owned TAK adapters, SitaWare and the NGC2 baseline, leaving an LLM ontology layer that solves a non-bottleneck and would fail deterministic conformance testing.

allied_extension: Marginally more compelling but still not a company: allied formats (ADatP-3, MIP, NVG, ASCA, STANAG 4586) are public or obtainable via national MoDs and CWIX/Bold Quest give cheap assessments, and a German founder can reach NATO DIANA/Bundeswehr channels.
